# Requirements

Ships Cody's product surface and the engine addons that make it sellable, superseding spec/cody task.7.1/8.6. Client: a full sibling app at /cody in apps/client (own sidebar, top bar, viewport, pages — the claude.ai vs claude.ai/code relationship to the Neo dashboard), web-first, with ONE engine truth disclosed in three mode tiers because modes are people groups: Prototype (vibe coder) = preview-first hero + outcome cards + one-button undo, no terminal/tree/diffs (single show-me-the-code escape hatch); Engineer (default) = adds the live waved task board, turn-in cards with real verification evidence, diff review, file tree, decision cards, named checkpoints; Architect = adds the terminal, live .cody/spec viewer, property-test results, full turn-in detail, git surface. Engine addons (user-locked 2026-07-03): anti-default enforcement by construction — greenfield Engineer/Architect runs are structurally blocked from wave 1 until a Stack Decision Record survives an anti-default adjudication lens citing rules/stack-selection doctrine, and UI work binds to a Design Language Record screened against a deterministic banned-AI-tells list (rules/web/design-quality.md); decision phases run hot with N divergent candidates judged, implementation runs cold. Plus: first-class spec ingestion (adopt a spec doc as the plan), mid-run steering + an answer channel for needs_input (SDR/DLR approval rides it — the human checkpoint lives at the two cheap-to-review expensive-to-get-wrong decisions, not on every task), HTTP-exposed snapshot/undo, worker ExtraTools wiring with screenshot-as-evidence for UI tasks, and preview-as-deliverable: on-demand Railway sandboxes (PRIVATE network) reverse-proxied by the router at /preview/{user} under the user's JWT — no public domains, VM stays outbound-quiet. Image gains codyd + local Postgres/Redis/SQLite + the baked quality toolchain (playwright browsers deliberately NOT baked — browser e2e runs in sandboxes); rules/ gains the stack-selection decision tables; skills/ gains the non-default framework playbooks.

## Requirement 1: The /cody sibling app surface

**User Story:** As a user, I want Cody to be its own app inside the Matrix client, so that coding work gets a purpose-built surface without disturbing the Neo dashboard.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. apps/client SHALL gain a /[locale]/cody route mounting a CodyApp with its own shell: left sidebar (projects, new project, recent runs, settings, back to Matrix), top bar (project name, mode chip, run status, stop), and a tier-driven main viewport; the Neo dashboard route SHALL be untouched.
2. THE surface SHALL comprise Workspace (hero), History (past runs + outcomes), and Settings (project mode, preview TTL) pages within the /cody shell.
3. THE surface SHALL reuse the existing client transport (apiFetch auth, SSE hub, seq-gap resume, replay-then-tail) with no new transport plumbing.
4. UI house rules SHALL hold: separation by background-color contrast only (never border strokes), no emojis/purple gradients/glow, single Paxeer Blue accent; vendored code rendering (Shiki code-block) SHALL be restyled to conform.
5. CONSUMER copy SHALL show the result, not the protocol: no orchestrator/worker/sheet jargon; the explanation register SHALL follow the project's mode.

## Requirement 2: Projects with project-level mode

**User Story:** As a beta tester, I want multiple projects each with its own mode, so that my prototype and my production build live side by side with the right ceremony each.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. codyd SHALL maintain a project registry mapping project id to name, workspace root (/workspace/<dir>), mode, and created_at; the bare /workspace SHALL remain the default project for retro-compat.
2. /chat, /workspace/*, the run ledger, spec files, and snapshots SHALL scope to the addressed project's root.
3. MODE SHALL be a project-level setting (set at creation, changeable between runs), not a per-message flag.
4. THE client SHALL provide project creation/selection in the /cody sidebar and mode setting in project Settings.

## Requirement 3: Live run surface — durable trace + live SSE

**User Story:** As a user, I want to watch Cody work and reopen the app to the same truth, so that progress is never lost to a closed tab.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A useCody reducer SHALL fold the Cody event family (plan.created, task.started/accepted/rejected/failed, sheet.authored, task.turnin, plan.completed, chat.assistant, message.complete) plus this feature's new events into a CodyRun model.
2. buildRunFromTrace SHALL rebuild the identical CodyRun from the durable trace on reopen (same fold as live), following the proven Neo pattern.
3. THE Workspace page SHALL render the run live: chat/steering rail, plan progress in the mode's register, turn-in cards (changes, verification evidence, honest gaps), and terminal status.
4. NEW event types (decision.stack, decision.design, decision.resolved, run.needs_input, preview.pending/ready/failed/expired, snapshot.created/restored, plan.adopted) SHALL be added to the SSE family and the durable-trace whitelist.

## Requirement 4: Mode-tiered disclosure — one engine truth, three tiers

**User Story:** As a vibe coder or an engineer, I want the surface to match who I am, so that I am neither drowned in machinery nor starved of evidence.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. PROTOTYPE SHALL render preview as the hero with outcome-language cards, a plain-language design-direction card, one-button undo, and NO terminal, file tree, or raw diffs; a single show-me-the-code escape hatch SHALL open the read-only viewer.
2. ENGINEER (default) SHALL add the waved task board as centerpiece, diff review pane, per-task verification evidence, file tree, SDR/DLR technical decision cards, and named checkpoint/restore.
3. ARCHITECT SHALL add the terminal (Architect-only), the live spec viewer (.cody/spec/requirements.md + tasks.md with checkbox state), property-test results, full turn-in detail, and the git surface (staged diff + proposed commit; the user drives the commit).
4. EVERY mode SHALL have: chat/steering, live progress, the needs-input prompt, stop, preview, what-changed summaries, run history, undo, and settings.
5. TIERS SHALL differ only in disclosure and register — never in the underlying run data or the constitution.

## Requirement 5: Code panes — file tree, viewer, diff review

**User Story:** As an engineer, I want to inspect the tree, read files, and review diffs, so that I can audit accepted work without leaving the surface.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE file tree SHALL render GET /workspace/tree (project-scoped) with truncation surfaced honestly.
2. THE read-only viewer SHALL render GET /workspace/file with Shiki highlighting restyled to the no-borders house rule.
3. THE diff pane SHALL render GET /workspace/diff (staged + unstaged + untracked) hunk-by-hunk as a passive audit surface; task-level blocking review is a non-goal.

## Requirement 6: Terminal — Architect only

**User Story:** As an architect, I want a terminal into my environment, so that I can poke the machine myself when I need to.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE terminal pane SHALL execute via POST /workspace/exec (bounded command-run, v1 is not a PTY) and render output with exit codes and duration.
2. THE terminal SHALL be present only in Architect-mode projects.

## Requirement 7: Preview — on-demand sandbox behind the router

**User Story:** As a user, I want to see my running app the moment Cody says it's ready, so that done means demonstrably working, not claimed.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a plan completes (or the user requests preview), codyd SHALL provision a Railway sandbox (PRIVATE network mode, same project/environment), deploy the project's current state, start its detected start command, health-probe it, and emit preview.ready with the proxied URL.
2. THE router SHALL add a /preview/{userID}/... path that authenticates the user's JWT (path user must match token user) and reverse-proxies to that user's registered preview target over the private network; previews SHALL never be world-readable and no sandbox public domain SHALL be required.
3. A TTL reaper SHALL destroy idle preview sandboxes (config knob, default 30m) and emit preview.expired; re-preview SHALL be a single client action.
4. THE sandbox client SHALL be Go-native (extending the router's Railway GraphQL transport) if the sandbox API permits, else a minimal Node sidecar in the image; the codyd-facing seam SHALL be identical either way.
5. WORKERS SHALL be able to request an ephemeral sandbox for browser-driven e2e (playwright runs in the sandbox, never in the user VM).
6. THE client preview pane SHALL render the proxied URL in all modes; in Prototype it SHALL be the hero viewport.

## Requirement 8: Stack Decision Record — gated anti-default stack selection

**User Story:** As the user, I want Engineer/Architect to pick the best-fitting stack like a senior engineer would, so that greenfield output never defaults to the path of least resistance.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. ON greenfield detection in Engineer/Architect, THE orchestrator SHALL author a durable Stack Decision Record before planning: requirements profile (app class, audience, deployment target, team context), 2-3 genuinely divergent candidate stacks, fit rationale per candidate citing rules/stack-selection, and a pick.
2. THE SDR SHALL pass the layered gate with an anti-default adjudication lens: a choice that would be identical regardless of the requirements SHALL be rejected.
3. WAVE 1 SHALL be structurally unreachable until the SDR is resolved (gate-accepted AND user-approved or user-overridden via the answer channel).
4. PROTOTYPE SHALL skip the SDR and default to the classic stack (Node/TS, Vite or Next, npm).
5. DEVIATIONS from the rules/stack-selection doctrine SHALL require explicit stated rationale in the SDR.

## Requirement 9: Design Language Record — gated anti-AI-default UI

**User Story:** As the user, I want UIs that no one can tell an AI made, so that Cody's frontend output is the opposite of the generic template look.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. FOR UI-bearing projects, THE orchestrator SHALL author a durable Design Language Record before the first UI task: style direction, typography, palette, spacing/layout system, motion posture, component idiom.
2. THE DLR SHALL pass a deterministic banned-defaults screen (rules/web/design-quality.md banned patterns plus the AI-tells list: untouched stock component themes, purple/indigo gradient heroes, glassmorphism blobs, emoji-in-UI, default framework blue) and an adjudication lens asking whether the output is distinguishable from AI-default.
3. EVERY subsequent UI task sheet SHALL carry the DLR as a constraint; THE acceptance gate SHALL reject turn-ins that drift from it.
4. IN Engineer/Architect the DLR SHALL be a blocking approve/override card; IN Prototype it SHALL surface as a plain-language design-direction card with a change-the-look affordance without blocking the run.

## Requirement 10: Creativity split — decision phases hot, implementation cold

**User Story:** As the user, I want bold decisions and precise implementation, so that divergence happens by construction, not by asking one lukewarm sample to be creative.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE mode tuple SHALL split Creativity into DecisionCreativity (hot) and ImplementationCreativity (cold, current values), plus a DecisionCandidates count (2-3).
2. SDR, DLR, and plan-shape authoring SHALL run at decision temperature generating N divergent candidates that are judged; worker implementation SHALL run cold.

## Requirement 11: Spec ingestion — adopt a spec document as the plan

**User Story:** As an engineer, I want to hand Cody an existing spec and have it execute it, so that my planning artifact is the plan, not a paraphrase of it.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. /chat SHALL accept a spec reference (workspace path or pasted document); THE planner SHALL adopt it: requirements map to acceptance grounding, tasks/waves derive from the document structure where present, and the ledger records the source via a plan.adopted event.
2. A run against an adopted spec SHALL be resumable like any plan (kill/restart resumes at the correct next task against the same adopted spec).
3. THE client new-run flow SHALL offer spec adoption (pick a workspace file or paste).

## Requirement 12: Steering + the answer channel

**User Story:** As a user, I want to redirect a live run and answer its questions, so that autonomy never means locked-out.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. POST /intents/{id}/answer SHALL resolve a needs_input stall with free text or a decision verdict (approve / override with payload); stop-and-ask and SDR/DLR approval SHALL both ride this channel.
2. POST /intents/{id}/steer SHALL fold a mid-run correction into the live run at the next orchestrator boundary — never interrupting a mid-flight worker; the orchestrator SHALL weigh the steer into subsequent sheets or re-plan remaining waves when invalidated.
3. THE client SHALL render the needs-input prompt in every mode and a steering affordance in the chat rail; run.needs_input and its resolution SHALL be durable trace events.

## Requirement 13: Worker ExtraTools + screenshot evidence

**User Story:** As the acceptance gate, I want workers to see what they built, so that design quality is verified, not asserted.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. codyd SHALL populate worker ExtraTools with the browser (shared browser service), fetch, and web-search bridges through the existing ExtraTools/ExtraDispatch seam.
2. UI-task sheets SHALL require a screenshot artifact in turn-in evidence; THE gate SHALL reject UI turn-ins without one; screenshots SHALL surface in the client's turn-in cards.

## Requirement 14: Undo — snapshots over HTTP

**User Story:** As a vibe coder, I want one button that puts things back, so that experimentation is never scary.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. codyd SHALL expose the existing Snapshotter: POST /workspace/snapshot (named), GET /workspace/snapshots, POST /workspace/restore; restore SHALL refuse while a worker is alive.
2. THE client SHALL render one-button undo (latest snapshot) in Prototype and named checkpoint/restore in Engineer/Architect; snapshot.created/restored SHALL be trace events.

## Requirement 15: Image completeness — codyd, local data stores, quality toolchain

**User Story:** As the operator, I want the per-user image to carry everything Cody's promise needs, so that a fresh environment codes at senior grade on first wake.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. deploy/railway SHALL build and supervise codyd beside the existing stack (entrypoint process + CODY_* env wiring + agents/cody.json present).
2. THE image SHALL bake PostgreSQL, Redis, and SQLite as exec-bridge-startable local services (no nested Docker on Railway).
3. THE image SHALL bake the quality toolchain: golangci-lint, ruff, eslint, prettier, tsc, vitest, cargo-clippy; playwright browsers SHALL NOT be baked (browser e2e runs in sandboxes).
4. THE sandbox client (Go binary or Node sidecar per req.7) SHALL ship in the image.

## Requirement 16: Rules + skills — the selection layer and the non-default playbooks

**User Story:** As the user, I want Cody's taste to be curated data, so that doctrine evolves by editing files, not retraining prompts.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. rules/stack-selection/ SHALL be authored as decision tables (app class to stack: chat/realtime -> React Router framework mode; content/marketing -> Astro/Next; internal enterprise -> Angular; high-throughput backend -> Go; correctness-critical -> Rust; ML-adjacent -> Python/uv; deviation demands rationale) and injected via the existing rules seam; the SDR gate SHALL cite it as doctrine.
2. skills/ SHALL gain framework playbooks for the non-default picks (Angular, React Router v7/Remix, Astro, SvelteKit), a Railway-deploy skill, a database-schema-design playbook if absent, and a toolchain-bootstrap skill (on-demand apt/mise install of long-tail stacks).

## Requirement 17: Real verification — no fakes

**User Story:** As the owner, I want every pillar proven against real code paths, so that the surface ships genuinely working.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. SDR/DLR structural tests: greenfield Engineer run cannot reach wave 1 without a resolved SDR; a default-stack SDR for an internal-enterprise profile is rejected by the anti-default lens; a banned-defaults DLR is rejected deterministically; a UI turn-in drifting from the accepted DLR is rejected; Prototype skips SDR.
2. DECISION gate round-trip: run pauses needs_input on SDR; /answer with override resolves; the plan proceeds against the override; trace replay is byte-identical.
3. STEERING: a mid-plan steer lands in the next authored sheet and never kills the live worker.
4. SPEC ingestion: a seeded SPEC.md adopts into a mapped plan; kill codyd mid-plan; resume continues against the adopted spec.
5. PREVIEW: sandbox lifecycle against recorded httptest fixtures; router /preview proxy integration test (JWT-authenticated request reaches a fake sandbox listener; cross-user path is 403; TTL reaper destroys + emits preview.expired).
6. UNDO: snapshot -> mutate -> restore round-trips bytes; restore refused while a worker is alive.
7. CLIENT: vitest proves buildRunFromTrace equals the live fold for the full event family including decisions/preview/needs-input; tier rendering asserted (Prototype hides terminal/tree/diff; Architect shows spec viewer + terminal).
8. SCREENSHOT evidence: a UI-task turn-in without a screenshot is rejected; with one, accepted — real gate, seeded sheet.
9. NO test SHALL substitute a stub/mock/fake for a real code path or type to manufacture a pass.
